Harkesh Manuja, J. (Oral)

By way of present petition filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of India read with Section
115 Cpc, prayer has been made for issuance of direction to the learned Executing Court to decide the
Execution No. 2022 dated 07.07.2022 titled as 'Pawan ' Kumar and others vs. State of Haryana and
another' within a time bound period and in terms of order dated 22.04.20 22.04.2021 21 passed by
the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No(s).1659 No(s).1659-1660 of 2021.
[2].

sentences.text: Admittedly, certain land owned by the petitioners was acquired vide notification dated 15.12.2006 and 14.12.2007 issued under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the 1894 Act') respectively, followed by an award dated 03.07.2009 passed by the Land Acquisition Collector, whereby the petitioners and other persons were granted compensation to the tune of Rs.20 lakhs per acre.

Feeling dissatisfied, dissatisfied the land owners filed petition under Section 18 of the 1894 Act, which was decided by the Reference Court vide award dated 05.07.2014.
1 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:000683 [3].

Aggrieved thereof, thereof the petitioners /

sentences.text:
Later the petitioners filed Execution Petition No.661// 2022 on 03.11.2022 .2022 before the learned Addl.
District & Sessions Judge, Rohtak and the same is now fixed for 30.01.2025 for making payment of compensation to the petitioners, however however,, till date, the enhanced amount of compensation has not been disbursed to the petitioner petitioners and other land owners.

[4]. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the peti petitioners tioners being aggrieved of the non-disbursal non disbursal of amount of compensation have filed the present revision petition for issuance of direction rection to the Executing Court concerned to decide the execution application expeditiously, in a time bound manner.
[5]. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the paper book.

[6]. A perusal of record shows that execution application (Annexure P-2) P filed by the petitioners on 03.11.2022 .2022 is still pending and the petitioners are waiting to get their amount of of compensation on the basis of order dated 16.03.2022 passed by this Court.

In Rahul S. Shah vs. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi and others reported as (2021) 6 SCC 418 the Hon'ble 'ble Supreme Court held as follows:
follows:-
"That the executing Court must dispose of execution proceedings within 6 months from the date of filing which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay."

entities.text: Rahul S. Shah vs. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi and others reported as (2021) 6 SCC 418
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of above, the Court of Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Rohtak (the Executing Court)
is requested to dispose of the Executing Petition 2 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:000683 /2022 as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of next 04 months from today, as any further delay is going to cause serious prejudice to the rights of the petitioners/land owners.
